newsitem.title: CANADA: StatsCan acreage data expected bullish wheat-trade.
newsitem.headline: StatsCan acreage data expected bullish wheat-trade.

text.p: Statistics Canada's second seeding intentions report for the 1997/98 (Aug/July) crop year due Friday may well prove bullish for wheat prices and slightly bearish for canola, grain trade analysts said.
"It'll be a little friendly to wheat because that acreage was going to be down anyway and it'll be down even more," due to unseeded Alberta fields, LFG analyst Rob Dzisiak said.
StatsCan's acreage report is due at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT Friday, updating its first intentions report issued April 30 based on a survey of farmers at the end of March.
For Friday's report, StatsCan surveyed Canadian farmers between May 26 and June 4.
Analysts expected StatsCan to reduce all wheat area in western Canada to 27.7 million acres from it's last report of 28.2 million acres on April 30.
Alberta Agriculture on June 17 said 600,000 to 800,000 acres in the central Peace River Valley and the Athabasca crop district would not be seeded due to the cool, wet spring.
"StatsCan isn't going to reflect unseeded acres in Alberta because when the survey was taken, farmers had intentions of seeding that," Continental Grain Co analyst Greg Kostal said.
The unseeded area was intended for wheat and canola.

"People are shifting away from wheat because farmers are carrying more inventories into the new crop year, so if you've got it in your bin, why grow it in your fields," United Grain Growers analyst Mike Jubinville said.

The Canadian Wheat Board in March said it deferred sales of 1.5 million tonnes of wheat to the coming crop year due to a backlog of ships at Pacific ports which cost it more than C$15 million in demurrage fines.
Analysts expected canola area across the Prairies to rise to 12.1 to 12.6 million acres in Friday's report. The estimates exceeded StatsCan's April 30 forecast of 11.6 million acres.

Canola acres were expected to gain on wheat, a view reflected in an 8.2 percent drop in July Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola to C$388 a tonne Tuesday from C$424 April 24 while No1 Canada Western Red Spring wheat futures fell 2.7 percent in the same period.

The Canadian Wheat Board's May 22 outlook set No1 CWRS at C$171-201 a tonne in-store St. Lawrence/Vancouver from C$176-206 but the price outlook was expected to be cut further due to U.S. harvest pressure and good production prospects in U.S. hard and soft red wheats, analysts said.
The CWB is due to revise its monthly price forecast on Thursday at 1400 CDT/1900.
Trade expectations set Prairie barley area at 11.9 to 12.15 million acres, compared to StatsCan's April 30 forecast of 11.9 million acres.
Analysts expected oats area of about 5.15 million acres versus StatsCan's April projection of 4.9 million acres.
The trade also expected the flax area estimate to drop to 2.05 million acres from StatsCan's April 30 forecast of 2.3 million acres.
